samples.evidence: The fix converts a falsy resolved color to a fallback in `paint-layout.ts:389/558` and `color.ts:75/80`, but the parallel table text path still uses `??`: `const runTextColor = defaultColorResolver(style.color) ?? Theme.defaultColor;` (table-renderer.ts:457) and `ctx.fillStyle = defaultColorResolver(cellBlock.inlines[0]?.style.color) ?? Theme.defaultColor;` (table-renderer.ts:564). `defaultColorResolver('')` returns `''` (color.ts:16 `if (typeof c === 'string') return c;`), so `??` keeps `''` and `ctx.fillStyle = ''` is ignored by canvas — the run keeps whatever the previous pass set. In this very function the immediately preceding pass sets `ctx.fillStyle = focused ? Theme.selectionColor : Theme.selectionColorInactive` (table-renderer.ts:442), which is exactly the failure mode issue #728 describes. samples.summary: Collapsing '' to `undefined` after the resolver bypasses theme-aware fallback, painting legacy cleared runs in the docs default color on themed slides
samples.evidence: `const resolvedColor = resolveColor(style.color) || undefined;` then `let textColor = resolvedColor ?? theme.defaultColor;`. For slides the injected resolver (packages/slides/src/view/canvas/text-renderer.ts:52-63 `makeColorResolver`) maps a *missing* color to the deck theme's text color (`themeText`), but a legacy `''` reaches the resolver, comes back `''`, and is turned into the docs `theme.defaultColor` (near-black) instead of being re-resolved as "no color" through the theme. On a dark deck theme, runs whose color was cleared before this fix paint dark-on-dark (effectively invisible) rather than in the theme text color. The correct handling is to fall back to `resolveColor(undefined)`. The same shape appears at renderListMarker (paint-layout.ts:558, `resolveColor(colorSource) || theme.defaultColor`) and in resolveColorAtPosition (packages/docs/src/model/color.ts:75/80, `|| fallback` where the slides caller passes the docs `Theme.cursorColor`, text-box-editor.ts:578-583), so the caret over such a run also reverts to the docs cursor color on a dark slide.

samples.summary: `underlineColor` still uses `??`, so an empty-string underline color would leave the previous strokeStyle in effect
samples.evidence: `ctx.strokeStyle = resolveColor(style.underlineColor) ?? textColor;` — same class of bug the diff fixes for `color`: `''` survives `??` and `strokeStyle = ''` is ignored by canvas, so the underline is stroked in whatever color the previous pass left. `underlineColor` is a `StoredColor` (types.ts:157) that can arrive from PPTX import (packages/slides/src/import/pptx/text.ts:505) and from clipboard/HTML paths, so an empty value is not structurally impossible even though no toolbar currently writes one.

samples.summary: No migration/normalisation strips the `color: ""` attribute the old Reset button already wrote into persisted documents
samples.evidence: The UI fix only prevents *new* empty-string colors; `parseInlineStyle` still materialises `if ('color' in attrs) style.color = attrs.color;` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:176) for existing docs, and `serializeInlineStyle` (line 121) round-trips `''` back out. Every consumer must therefore be `''`-tolerant forever; the diff only hardened three of them, leaving table-renderer.ts:457/564 broken and the exported paths relying on incidental truthiness. I searched for any normalisation/migration of stored colors and found none: no `migrat`/`normalizeColor` handling for the color attribute, `wrapLegacyColor` (model/color.ts:45) is an identity function, and `normalizeInlines` (store/block-helpers.ts) merges runs without sanitising style values.

verdict.reason: Verified in the repo: table-renderer.ts:457 and :564 still use `??` against `defaultColorResolver`, which returns '' verbatim for a stored empty-string color (color.ts:16). `ctx.fillStyle = ''` is ignored by canvas, so cell text/list markers keep the previous pass's fill — and renderTableContent's own contract (table-renderer.ts:244-248) plus the in-loop selection fill (table-renderer.ts:442) mean that prior fill is the cell background or selection color. The parallel body path was fixed to `||` with explicit issue-#728 comments (paint-layout.ts:389, paint-layout.ts:558, color.ts:75/80), and the task doc explicitly relies on the renderer guard instead of a migration (20260812-docs-font-color-reset-todo.md:47-52), while stored '' round-trips through yorkie-doc-store.ts:121/176 into table cell inlines (yorkie-doc-store.ts:361). renderTableContent is on the live render path (doc-canvas.ts:525, :733). Real, unguarded, in-lane.

finding.summary: Collapsing '' to `undefined` after the resolver bypasses theme-aware fallback, painting legacy cleared runs in the docs default color on themed slides
finding.evidence: `const resolvedColor = resolveColor(style.color) || undefined;` then `let textColor = resolvedColor ?? theme.defaultColor;`. For slides the injected resolver (packages/slides/src/view/canvas/text-renderer.ts:52-63 `makeColorResolver`) maps a *missing* color to the deck theme's text color (`themeText`), but a legacy `''` reaches the resolver, comes back `''`, and is turned into the docs `theme.defaultColor` (near-black) instead of being re-resolved as "no color" through the theme. On a dark deck theme, runs whose color was cleared before this fix paint dark-on-dark (effectively invisible) rather than in the theme text color. The correct handling is to fall back to `resolveColor(undefined)`. The same shape appears at renderListMarker (paint-layout.ts:558, `resolveColor(colorSource) || theme.defaultColor`) and in resolveColorAtPosition (packages/docs/src/model/color.ts:75/80, `|| fallback` where the slides caller passes the docs `Theme.cursorColor`, text-box-editor.ts:578-583), so the caret over such a run also reverts to the docs cursor color on a dark slide.

verdict.reason: The claimed code exists verbatim and behaves as described. paint-layout.ts:389-390 collapses a resolver result of '' to undefined and then falls back to the docs `theme.defaultColor`, bypassing the theme-aware "no color" path. The slides resolver (slides/src/view/canvas/text-renderer.ts:52-63) only maps null/undefined and '#000000' to the deck's `themeText`; an empty string falls through line 57 and is returned as '', so it can never reach the theme fallback. Slides callers pass only `colorResolver` and no `theme` (text-renderer.ts:242; docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:597-602), so `theme` is the docs DefaultTheme whose `defaultColor` is docs ink (docs/src/view/theme.ts:49,80) — near-black on a dark deck theme. Empty-string colors are a documented legacy reality (paint-layout.ts:545-549, test/view/paint-layout.test.ts:192-200, frontend color-reset.test.ts:1-12) and the picker that wrote them is used by the slides toolbar (frontend/src/app/slides/toolbar/text-edit-section.tsx). No upstream normalization removes them: prepareBlocksForLayout only calls normalizeBlockStyle, a block-style spread (docs/src/model/types.ts:272-274) that never touches inline colors. The same `|| fallback` shape is present at paint-layout.ts:558 and model/color.ts:75,80 with the slides caret caller passing docs Theme.cursorColor (docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:578-583). No refutation ground applies: the code is present, unguarded, and wrong-fallback rendering that can paint text invisibly is within the correctness lane.
